problems.title: AI context loss
problems.description: Agents re-explain themselves every session. No memory, no continuity across runs.

problems.title: Agent setup complexity
problems.description: MCP, Claude, and similar tools are too technical for non-developers. Setup friction kills adoption.

problems.title: Calorie tracking still broken
problems.description: cal.ai and MyFitnessPal exist but tracking sauces, mixed dishes, and custom meals remains unreliable.

problems.title: Workout tracking is too manual
problems.description: Logging sets, reps, and progress requires too much manual input. Should be more automated.

problems.title: Scheduling and habit adherence
problems.description: Making a schedule is easy. Actually sticking to it is unsolved. No tool makes routines truly stick.

problems.title: Marketing automation is still dumb
problems.description: Codex automations and generic tools don't drive real traction. Need a CMO-level agent that actually works with proof.

problems.title: Warm leads go cold silently
problems.description: Sales threads open, no follow-up system, no signal for who to re-engage. Warm leads die without notice.

problems.title: ICP buying signals vanish into noise
problems.description: Intent signals from Reddit, Twitter, and LinkedIn disappear in the feed within hours. No structured capture.

problems.title: Content distribution is still manual
problems.description: One diary entry or blog post needs to be manually adapted to X, LinkedIn, Reddit, and your blog. Prose distribution is unsolved.

problems.title: Blog publishing is too many steps
problems.description: Publishing posts, uploading images, generating OG images, and deploying takes too long. Most CLI tools are incomplete.

problems.title: Video editing takes too long
problems.description: Creating polished short-form video content requires too much time and skill. No AI tool fully solves this end-to-end.

problems.title: AI can't write in your voice
problems.description: Current AI writing forgets your style, tone, and history between sessions. No continuity or authentic voice persistence.

problems.title: Skill files have no home
problems.description: No marketplace or registry to find, share, or discover quality skill files for AI agents. Everyone builds from scratch.

problems.title: AI context costs too much
problems.description: Long agent sessions burn through context fast. Inference pricing surprises every month. No good compression layer beyond basic skill files.

problems.title: Agentic OS / terminal-native workspace
problems.description: Need a fully AI-readable operating environment like IBX but in the terminal. Agents can read and act on the entire state.

problems.title: 3D websites are still too hard to build
problems.description: AI website builders can't generate quality 3D experiences like igloo.inc. Gap between design intent and output is massive.

problems.title: AI game maker space is untouched
problems.description: Website and app generators exist, but a high-quality AI game maker has no clear winner. High viral and monetization potential.

problems.title: Learning to code in the agentic era is broken
problems.description: Courses still teach traditional coding. The real gap is learning to build with agents, not just write functions.

problems.title: No persistent personal knowledge layer
problems.description: Need a system that knows and remembers everything, accessible via CLI and chat integrations (Discord, Slack, etc.).

problems.title: Shared agent task layer for teams
problems.description: A multiplayer execution queue where teammates dump blockers in natural language and an agent organizes, prioritizes, and assigns. No Jira config.

problems.title: ICP research is still manual
problems.description: Brain-style tools that do ICP research automatically only work for one person. Everyone else does it manually.

problems.title: Strategy drift goes undetected
problems.description: Actions stop matching stated direction and nobody flags it. No system keeps execution aligned with strategy in real time.

problems.title: Motion vs. progress is a recurring bug
problems.description: Doing a lot but not moving the needle. No fast signal for whether daily output actually advances the goal.

problems.title: Standup is still a broken ritual
problems.description: Tools just move the same bad question to a different channel. State that should be visible has to be reconstructed every day.

problems.title: Slack decisions disappear
problems.description: PR context expires, decisions made in Slack vanish. Institutional knowledge degrades continuously.

problems.title: 25+ apps, no single status view
problems.description: No dashboard or CLI showing all deployed apps, their status, health, and last-touched date.

problems.title: Open source gap between code and running system
problems.description: Repos represent a complete system but the setup effort is the entire product. Nobody can onboard without the author.

problems.title: No fast way to validate problem frequency before building
problems.description: Built Huesly for a monthly problem. Spent 2 months on Go infrastructure before talking to a user. No tool distinguishes daily pain from occasional annoyance.

problems.title: Reach vs. conversion are completely different signals
problems.description: 100k Reddit impressions, 4 signups. No tool clearly separates distribution signal from conversion signal.

problems.title: Channel dilution looks like leverage
problems.description: Spreading across 5 channels simultaneously and owning none of them. No system enforces channel focus.

problems.title: Pitching before listening
problems.description: First-wave outreach was a mini landing page nobody asked for. No system forces listening mode before selling.

problems.title: Development environment barrier for low-resource learners
problems.description: Learned on an iPad, SSHing into a VPS. Real development is inaccessible without the right hardware.

problems.title: Offline-first is still an afterthought
problems.description: Unreliable school internet. Most developer tools assume connectivity. Offline-first tooling doesn't exist.

problems.title: Context switching between school and startup destroys deep work
problems.description: No system manages the cognitive cost of switching between high-stakes domains within the same day.

problems.title: Productivity system becomes procrastination
problems.description: Over-engineered the IBX system so badly it became the thing being procrastinated with. The system became the work.
